paper.geometry: 3-turn SYMMETRIC OCTAGONAL spiral, r_out 218 um, W 30 um, S 14 um, TopMetal2 with a TopMetal1 underpass
paper.status: CONTEXT ONLY -- no gate in this study compares to it

deviations.what: square spiral instead of the paper's octagon
deviations.why: the differentiable body-fitted metric of rfx.fdfd.spiral is built on axis-aligned breakpoints (rect_spiral); gds.octagonal_spiral exists but spiral.py has no breakpoint map for it
deviations.effect: a square of the same r_out has more metal and a longer conductor than the inscribed octagon, so its L is HIGHER at equal r_out; it is a different device, not a discretisation of the paper's

deviations.what: single-ended spiral with an underpass instead of a symmetric (two-winding) differential inductor
deviations.why: rect_spiral builds one winding; SpiralSpec has no symmetric topology
deviations.effect: L_diff here is the series inductance of one winding between two terminals, not the differential inductance of two interleaved ones

deviations.what: silicon 120 um thick over a PEC ground instead of ~190 um
deviations.why: the vertical grid is layer-uniform (gds.z_lines) and every 60 um silicon cell costs 3 x 43 x 44 unknowns
deviations.effect: MEASURED, both by the FDFD (two thicknesses at the coarse level) and by the referee's ground image at 60/120/190/300 um: see B.t_si_sensitivity

deviations.what: TopVia2 widened from ~0.85 um to 2 um
deviations.why: leontovich_validity divides the skin depth by the THINNEST metal slab; at 0.85 um the via, a 30 um square carrying the series current between the layers, would set that number instead of the 2 um underpass
deviations.effect: the M2-M1 centre separation becomes 4.5 um instead of 3.35 um (+34 %), slightly changing the underpass mutual

deviations.what: passivation permittivity lumped into the oxide's 4.1 (public 6.6)
deviations.why: SmallStack has one oxide permittivity for the whole back end
deviations.effect: a 1.5 um layer directly above the strip is 4.1 instead of 6.6: the strip's shunt capacitance to the air side is slightly low, which raises the self-resonance a little

deviations.what: the Leontovich sheet is used outside its delta << t range
deviations.why: the pipeline has no finite-thickness skin-effect metal model
deviations.effect: absolute Q at 2.45 GHz is not a validated number: see B.leontovich for delta/t

calibration.note: t_si = 60 um configuration, run once before the study to size it; with three LU factors live the footprint is 15.3 GB, which is why every solve in the study keeps ONE

meta.protocol_source: validation/fdfd/spiral_convergence.py (study D2): uniform-current volumetric metal sigma = 3e6 at 100 MHz, vacuum dielectrics, pad_cells = 4 graded wall cells, area-exact corner convention, primary referee L(strip) - L(short's bridge)

fixture.dut: SQUARE 3-turn spiral (rfx.fdfd.gds.rect_spiral) on TopMetal2 with a TopMetal1 underpass -- NOT the paper's octagon, see the module doc

referee.what: Greenhouse partial inductance with a PEC ground image; PRIMARY convention L(strip) - L(short's bridge), area-exact corners, reference plane at the lead-column footprint centre (D2's protocol, bridge construction reused)

mohan_wheeler.what: SECONDARY sanity number: Mohan's modified-Wheeler fit for a SQUARE spiral (Mohan et al., JSSC 34(10) 1999, eq. 2; 2-3 % typical and ~8 % worst-case error against field solvers). The fit has NO ground plane, so the number to read it against is the referee's free-space strip, not the ground-imaged one.
mohan_wheeler.d_in_definition: inner edge of the innermost complete turn (the inner extension to the via sits inside the hole and is not a turn)

R1.quantity: FDFD de-embedded L_diff at 100 MHz vs the PRIMARY referee L(strip) - L(short's bridge) on the same square geometry; no FDFD-side correction applied
R1.criterion: the W/2 gap must be within 3 points of D2's small-spiral W/2 gap (-0.1203), i.e. the deficit at RFIC scale is the known strip cross-section discretisation bias and nothing new

wall_correction.what: the same W/1 model under part A's protocol with the four side walls pushed from 4 to 8 graded cells (431 -> 1356 um from the axis; the PEC lid is pinned at 3 padding cells in both). D2's wall gate on the 104 um spiral moved L by +0.114 % for pad 4 -> 8; this device is four times larger inside the same margin + padding, so the residual is larger and it is measured here rather than assumed.

R2.deembedded_note: reciprocity and passivity are gated on the three SOLVED S-matrices (dut, open, short). The de-embedded S is a post-processing construct (Y_short - Y_open inverted), not a solver output, so its singular values are REPORTED, not gated.

wall_ladder.what: least squares of L (and Q) against 1/wall_distance over the three pads: the intercept is the wall-free limit

R2.wall_interpretation: pad 4 -> 6 moves L by +0.983 %, pad 6 -> 8 by +0.041 %: the box is converged from pad 6 on, so the wall-free L is the pad-8 value to about 0.04 % and the pad-4 model used by parts A, B and C is 1.02 % LOW from the side walls alone. The 1/distance fit over all three points has a 0.25 % residual and is reported only for completeness.

R3.note: jax.grad of the FDFD metric against a 4th-order central difference of the SAME discrete model; 1 %% steps move L by ~1 %% and Q by ~1 %%, far above the ~1e-9 LU noise floor

paper_context.what: arXiv 2607.08852, a 3-turn SYMMETRIC OCTAGONAL spiral; CONTEXT ONLY, never a gate (this DUT is a square, single-ended spiral on a 120 um substrate over a PEC ground)

R5.what: largest N, per-fixture factorisation+solve wall time, peak memory per process; every level actually run. Wall times are UPPER BOUNDS: this machine ran a second agent throughout.

scaling.what: single-fixture (DUT only) solve time and factor memory against N on one geometry, N moved by the wall padding alone; the fit is the basis of the W/3 cost projection
scaling.fit_note: least squares on log N over N = 45744..85785 (5 points): seconds ~ N^2.04, peak process footprint ~ N^2.12

single_call_path.what: one spiral.solve_spiral call for all three fixtures (forward_point: the FD stencils, and the same path the design loop's value_and_grad takes) against solve_split's three single-fixture calls. The metrics are BITWISE the same (gated in tests/test_fdfd_rfic_spiral.py); the peak memory is not, because the three fixtures' assembled operators are live in one XLA program.

w3_cost_projection.what: extrapolation, NOT a measurement: the W/3 model is built (N exact) but never solved on this machine

A.what: absolute L at 100 MHz under D2's validated protocol (uniform-current volumetric metal sigma = 3e6, vacuum dielectrics, pad_cells = 4, area-exact corners) against the PRIMARY referee L(strip) - L(bridge); no FDFD-side correction applied

w3_projection.what: the level the bar study called the 2 % point (3+ cells across W): built but NOT solved -- N and the extrapolated cost only

B.what: 2.45 GHz with a Leontovich metal sheet (sigma 3.05e7) and lossy silicon (sigma 2 S/m) and the real permittivities (eps_si 11.9, eps_ox 4.1)

t_si_sensitivity.what: L and Q against the substrate thickness at base_dx = W, 2.45 GHz: the fixture's PEC ground sits under the silicon, so the thickness is the ground-image distance and it is bought in whole 60 um cells

wall.note: pad_cells_z is pinned at 3 in both pads, so this gate moves the four SIDE walls only (431 -> 1356 um from the axis); the PEC lid stays at z = 622 um, i.e. 489 um above the top of TopMetal2. D2's wall gate moved the lid with the walls and measured the two together as +0.114 %.

ladder.what: least squares of L (and Q) against 1/wall_distance over the three pads: the intercept is the wall-free limit

leontovich.what: skin depth over the THINNEST metal slab of the stack; the Leontovich sheet needs it well below 1 and it is not -- absolute Q at 2.45 GHz is therefore not a validated number here (see the module doc)

pure_copper.note: the task's expected ~0.45 is delta/t for PURE copper (5.8e7 S/m) on the 3 um TopMetal2; the stack's 3.05e7 S/m gives a 1.36x larger skin depth

scaling.what: single-fixture (DUT only) solve time and factor memory against N on one geometry, N moved by the wall padding alone; the fit is the basis of the W/3 cost projection
scaling.fit_note: least squares on log N over N = 45744..85785 (5 points): seconds ~ N^2.04, peak process footprint ~ N^2.12

merged_runs.what: a sibling process that worked on disjoint items of this study (--only / --c-items / --fd-params) in parallel; its wall time is NOT added to this study's `seconds`, which is per-process
